The Semester Grade Point Average (SGPA) is calculated as the sum of the products of credit hours and grade points divided by the total credit hours registered in the semester. The formula is:

**SGPA = Sum(Credit_Hours * Grade_Points) / Sum(Credit_Hours)**

Source: prospectus-2026.md, Section 2. Grading Scheme and SGPA / CGPA Calculation, page 18.

Under the 2026 academic regulations, if a student repeats a course and earns a lower grade on the second attempt, **only the grade of the most recent attempt counts toward the CGPA calculation**, even if it is lower than the previous grade. All prior attempts remain visible on the official transcript but are annotated as repeated.

Source: academic-rules-2026.md | 5. Course Repetition & Prerequisite Failures | page 31
per_question.judge_reason: The answer accurately reflects the policy in section 5.2 that the most recent grade counts toward CGPA even if lower, and that prior attempts are annotated on the transcript.
